protocol: THE FIRST LABEL IN THIS SET NOT WRITTEN BY THE SAME PARTY AS THE
EXTRACTOR. That is what makes it worth more than the rest of the set
(LIMITATIONS.md 0b), and why it is kept separate rather than pooled.
All 28 distinct values were checked against page 32's text layer and are
present. The label omits the 'Shares used in computing earnings per share'
block (15,343,783 / 15,408,095 and prior years), which is a scope choice by
the labeller, not a transcription error -- those rows exist on the page.
notes: This is a SEMANTIC label, and it differs from a raw_text label in three
ways that the scorer has to respect rather than penalise:
1. ROW LABELS ARE FLATTENED. 'Net sales - Products' is one row here. The
page prints a section row 'Net sales:' with an indented 'Products'
beneath it, so a raw_text label has two rows where this has one. The
extractor recovers the same fact as row_label_path = ['Net sales:',
'Products'], which is why rows are matched on the JOINED label path
2. VALUES CARRY NO CURRENCY SYMBOL. The page cell literally reads
'$ 294,866'; this label reads '294,866'. Comparing these as strings
would fail on a cell the extractor got exactly right, so semantic mode
3. PERIODS ARE SHORT-FORM. '2024' here, 'September 28, 2024' on the page.
The brief scores both notions -- 'Exact match on raw_text; scored
separately on normalized_value' -- so both label types are kept. See
apple_p032_income_statement.json for the raw_text view of the same table.
